samples.summary: `unwrapJson` now swallows parse failures and falls back to `detachYorkieValue`, silently degrading data for 6 pre-existing call sites instead of failing loudly
samples.evidence: The diff changes the shared helper from `return JSON.parse(str)` to `try { parseJsonSnapshot(str) } catch { return detachYorkieValue(value) }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:21-25). Existing consumers not in the diff: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts (chart read), packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts, packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:59-68 (`readSlidesRoot` unwraps `themes/masters/layouts/slides/guides`), packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts. `detachYorkieValue` only preserves array-ness when `Array.isArray(value)` is true (yorkie-json.ts:168); a Yorkie array proxy that fails that test is walked by `Object.entries` and comes back as an object with numeric keys. On the fallback path `readSlidesRoot` would then return `slides`/`layouts` as objects (breaking the CLI/`slide-ops` consumers that call `.length`/`findIndex`), and worse, `tabs.controller.duplicate` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:245) feeds the `unwrapJson` result straight into `duplicateTab`, which WRITES it into the CRDT as the new worksheet — persisting `rowOrder`/`colOrder` as objects that the frontend reads as arrays (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts). Previously the throw surfaced as a 500 and nothing was written. Fix belongs on the new fallback in yorkie-json.ts (keep throwing, or make the fallback array-preserving).

samples.summary: Server-authored notifications store the raw mention markup as `preview`; the existing pipeline's other writer flattens it first, so the inbox will render `@[ada](7)` for API-authored comments
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications` passes `preview: comment.body` verbatim. The pre-existing writer of the same endpoint/service converts first: packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:35-37 (`preview()` = `mentionBodyToPlainText(body).slice(0, 200)`), and `mentionBodyToPlainText` (packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:124) turns `@[name](id)` into `@name`. `NotificationService.sanitizePreview` (packages/backend/src/notification/notification.service.ts:67) only strips control chars and caps length — it does not strip mention markup — so the notification list UI, which has only ever received flattened previews, now shows raw markup for agent-authored mentions.

samples.summary: The mention regex, `toUserId`, and the whole `planCommentNotifications` rule are re-implemented in the backend beside the existing frontend copy — two implementations of one contract that will drift
samples.evidence: Backend `MENTION_RE = /@\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]*)\)/g` and `toUserId` duplicate packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:24 (`/@\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)/g`) and packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:29-33; the plan rule duplicates notify.ts:50-114. The two writers now both decide recipients for the same pipeline, so a change to the mention encoding (mentions.ts `serializeMention`) or the reply/mention de-dupe rule must be made twice, with nothing tying them together.

samples.summary: The published REST API reference still describes the pre-change v1 surface: `/content` gated to doc/slides/note, and no comments, per-slide, worksheet-image or tab delete/move/duplicate routes
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:85 lists `Document content (/content) | doc / slides / note` (board is now accepted, docs-content.controller.ts:108-116) and the endpoint index at :76-96 plus the tab section at :343-388 document only `GET/POST /tabs` and `PATCH /tabs/:tid`. Nothing documents `DELETE /tabs/:tid`, `POST /tabs/:tid/move|duplicate`, `GET|PUT /tabs/:tid/images`, `GET /documents/:did/layouts`, `POST /documents/:did/slides…`, or the whole `/comments` tree added here. The doc-path CI check only verifies backticked paths in top-level docs/design/*.md, so nothing catches this.

samples.summary: CLI documentation enumerates the tab verbs as create/rename only and omits every command this change adds (tabs delete/move/duplicate, sheets images, slides layouts/slide, comments, board)
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:377-395 documents `sheets tabs list|create|rename` as the tab surface. `packages/cli/README.md` and `docs/design/cli.md` carry the same command inventory (both matched a grep for `sheets.tabs.rename`). The new commander groups registered in packages/cli/src/cli.ts:35-36 and packages/cli/src/commands/sheets.ts:32 appear only in the schema registry, so the human-facing docs now understate the surface; no lane checks command coverage (packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts has no registry↔commander completeness assertion).

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies a pivot-output tab's `kind: 'pivot'` and its `pivotTable`, creating a second output tab bound to the same source — a state no editor path produces and which the frontend recompute owns
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` copies `source.kind` into the new `TabMeta` and copies the worksheet wholesale (`{ ...worksheet, comments: {} }`), including `pivotTable.sourceTabId`. The frontend treats `root.tabs[tabId]?.kind === 'pivot'` as a recomputed, read-only output (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:251), so the duplicate's grid is overwritten on the next recompute; and the new `resolveDelete` will now report the copy as a pivot dependent, blocking deletion of the source until both are removed (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:83-92). The frontend has no duplicate-tab action at all (only `deleteTabWithDependents` / `handleMoveTab` in packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:468-573), so this shape is reachable only through the new route.

samples.summary: The CLI's duplicated `SheetImage` type marks `originalWidth`/`originalHeight` optional while the engine type requires them
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:127-139 declares `originalWidth?: number; originalHeight?: number;` whereas the canonical `SheetImage` in packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:34-45 requires both. The server defaults them (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts:65-72) so nothing breaks today, but a `sheets images get | sheets images set` round trip typed against the CLI copy will drift from the engine shape.

samples.summary: The comments controller throws NotFoundException from inside `doc.update`, contradicting the convention the sibling controller in this same change documents
samples.evidence: `mutateThread`/`deleteThread`/`deleteComment` run their `mutate` callback inside `doc.update` and throw from it (comments.controller.ts:388-400, 403-432, 455-465). packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-images.controller.ts:100-104 states the opposite convention explicitly ("Checked *before* doc.update rather than inside it: throwing from within the update leaves an aborted change on a document this request should not have touched"). In practice `mutateMap` pre-verifies the thread so the inner throw is near-unreachable, which is why this is a nit rather than a bug.

Existing consumers not in the diff: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts (chart read), packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts, packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:59-68 (`readSlidesRoot` unwraps `themes/masters/layouts/slides/guides`), packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts. `detachYorkieValue` only preserves array-ness when `Array.isArray(value)` is true (yorkie-json.ts:168); a Yorkie array proxy that fails that test is walked by `Object.entries` and comes back as an object with numeric keys. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: yorkie-json.ts:21-25 wraps parseJsonSnapshot in a try/catch that swallows any parse failure and returns detachYorkieValue(value), where parseJsonSnapshot (109-121) would otherwise rethrow a real SyntaxError. detachYorkieValue preserves array-ness only when Array.isArray(value) (line 168) and otherwise rebuilds via Object.entries/fromEntries (176-181), so a proxy failing that test degrades to an object with numeric keys. Consumers outside the diff are real and unguarded: slides-tree.ts:64-68 returns those values directly as typed arrays (75-79); tabs.controller.ts:249 passes the unwrapped worksheet to duplicateTab at line 259, and tab-ops.ts:167-168 spreads it straight into root.sheets[newTabId] inside doc.update with no shape validation, so a degraded value is persisted instead of the previous fail-loud 500. Other consumers at worksheet-charts.controller.ts:71, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:75/121, worksheet-images.controller.ts:81, board-tree.ts:57-58. No guard re-validates the result, so 'already-guarded' does not apply; this is a behaviour change to a shared exported symbol with unconsidered consumers including a CRDT write path — in-lane and blocking at major.

finding.summary: New `slides.slide.delete` reuses the alias `slide.delete`, which an earlier entry (`slides.delete`, delete the whole deck) already claims — `getCommandSchema` returns the first match, so `slide.delete` still resolves to the destructive document delete.
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:281 — `slides.delete` (safety: 'destructive', 'Delete a slide deck') declares `aliases: ['slide.delete', 'deck.delete', 'decks.delete']`. The new entry at :395 declares `aliases: ['slide.delete', 'deck.slide.delete']`. Resolution is `registry.find((c) => c.name === name)` then `registry.find((c) => c.aliases?.includes(name))` (registry.ts:1409-1413) — first-wins, so the new alias is dead and an agent asking for `slide.delete` meaning "remove one slide" is handed the schema for deleting the entire presentation. Same shadowing risk applies to the pattern generally; only this one collides today.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim is factually wrong. The new `slides.slide.delete` entry declares `aliases: ['deck.slide.delete']` (registry.ts:399) — it does NOT include `slide.delete`. Lines 395-398 are an explicit comment stating the alias was deliberately omitted because `slides.delete` already owns it and `getCommandSchema` resolves first-match. A repo-wide grep for the string `'slide.delete'` yields exactly one hit, registry.ts:281 (`slides.delete`), so there is no second claimant and no shadowed/dead alias. The first-match resolution at registry.ts:1413-1417 is as described, but there is no colliding alias for it to shadow. Additionally, the generalized risk is already mechanically guarded: packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts:164-183 walks every schema and asserts no alias is claimed twice and no alias equals a command name (`expect(collisions).toEqual([])`), which would fail the build if any such collision were reintroduced anywhere in the registry. Primary ground is not-present; the registry-wide test is a secondary guard.

finding.summary: Comment threads/replies/resolutions created through the new API never emit a notification: the notification pipeline is driven exclusively from the browser client, so participants and @mentioned users are silently not told about agent-authored comments.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:125 `notifyCommentEvent()` is what plans and POSTs `comment_added` / `comment_reply` / `thread_resolved` reports (via `reportCommentNotification`, packages/frontend/src/api/notifications.ts:94) into packages/backend/src/notification/notification.service.ts. The new `createThread` / `reply` / `setResolved` handlers write straight into the Yorkie CRDT and call nothing in NotificationService, so every notification type the dropdown shows for a comment is skipped for API writes. The controller's own docblock even asserts the author identity is "the same identity the notification routes hold a comment reporter to", but no report is made.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new comments API never emits notifications, but the controller does exactly that. comments.controller.ts:170-197 defines a private notify() helper that calls this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan) at line 188, driven by planCommentNotifications (lines 532-594) which produces comment_mention, comment_reply and thread_resolved DTOs -- the very types said to be skipped, including @mention parsing via MENTION_RE at line 504. It is invoked from createThread (pdf path line 290, sheet path line 320), reply (line 351), and setResolved (line 383, correctly only when resolving). The dependency is genuinely wired, not aspirational: NotificationService is injected at comments.controller.ts:103, api-v1.module.ts:31,50 imports NotificationModule, notification.module.ts:16 exports NotificationService, and notification.service.ts:113 implements createFromComment with the membership authorization and recipient cap the docblock describes. The controller's own spec asserts these calls (comments.controller.spec.ts:454,487,520,538) and asserts non-emission for reopen (line 549) and non-notifiable actors (line 563). The reviewer's cited search of packages/backend/src for "comment" would necessarily have surfaced line 188, so the evidence as stated does not hold.

finding.summary: `apply()` assigns the entire `root.slides` array (round-tripped and migrated through `MemSlidesStore`) for a single-slide operation, clobbering any concurrent per-slide/per-element edit the live editor made between the read and the write — contrary to the stated rationale that these verbs avoid whole-deck rewrites.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts mutates slides/elements granularly inside `doc.update` (per-element field writes), which is what makes concurrent editing converge. The new path does `doc.update((root) => { root.slides = result.slides; })` where `result.slides` came from `new MemSlidesStore(document)` — and `MemSlidesStore` clones + `migrateDocument`s on both construction and `read()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:140-157), so every slide object in the deck is replaced wholesale, not just the one added/moved/deleted. Any collaborator edit landing during the request is lost, which is exactly the failure mode `PUT .../content` has and that this controller's docblock claims to avoid.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `apply()` never assigns a deck array: inside `doc.update` it does `if (!root.slides) root.slides = []` (initialize-if-absent) and then `applySlideChange(slides, result.change)` (slides.controller.ts:186-191). `applySlideChange` (slide-ops.ts:92-133) performs a single granular mutation — one `splice` for insert/insert-after/remove, or `moveFront`/`moveAfterByIndex` in-place reorder for move — on the live CRDT array. `SlideOpResult` (slide-ops.ts:47-61) has no `slides` field, so the quoted `root.slides = result.slides` cannot exist; a repo-wide grep for `result.slides` finds it only in slides-tree.spec.ts assertions. The MemSlidesStore round trip in addSlide/duplicateSlide (slide-ops.ts:162-192) is used only to construct the one new Slide object that is spliced in; the clone's other slides are discarded. The only whole-array assignment in the repo is writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:105), whose sole non-test caller is the pre-existing whole-deck route docs-content.controller.ts:238; slides.controller.ts imports only readSlidesRoot (lines 19-22) and never calls writeSlidesRoot. Hence there is no lost-update/clobbering path at the cited location.
